character: Mel: everyday Kiwi woman, late 30s, the owner-builder in this skit (fictional, as are the roofer, the house and the Hamilton job; the video carries an 'A skit · names made up' chip until the thread ends). Dry and quietly amused at the paperwork and a little at herself (the third text says 'sorry, me again'), never at the roofer: he is busy on a job in Queenstown and 'fair enough' is meant. The hunt is read like a flat incident report, each place shorter and flatter than the last. General NZ accent, never a caricature, no announcer lift, no exclamation marks. Product lines are second-person or neutral tips ('You check it. You tick it.'), never 'I use it' or a result claim, so an AI voice can never read as a customer testimonial.

lines.on_screen: Dusk still of the finished house ('Illustrative footage', slow push); headline 'Everything's finished.' from frame 0; the move-in list 'MOVE IN BY CHRISTMAS · HAMILTON' is up by 0.15 and ticks Painted, Carpets down, Final inspection passed, Electrical CoC (0.25–0.84)
lines.delivery: Quietly pleased, like telling a mate over the fence; it says exactly what the headline says. Small lift on 'finished', no announcer energy. Out by 0.95, just as the last line goes red (0.85).

lines.on_screen: 'Record of Work — Roofing' turns red with an ✗ (0.85), shakes and gets a marker ring (0.95–1.30); red box 'Except one bit of paper.' slams in (0.91–1.05) and holds
lines.delivery: The turn. Same voice, all the pleasure drained out. Tiny pause after 'Except', 'one bit of paper' dead level. Out by 2.45, before the whip (2.42–2.62).

lines.on_screen: 'SEARCH 1 · Inbox.'; a generic mail search types 'record of work' (2.80–3.36) and comes back 'No results' (3.48)
lines.delivery: Incident-report flat. One word, falling. Leave the 'No results' to land in silence.

lines.on_screen: 'SEARCH 2 · Garage.'; a cardboard box marked 'HOUSE STUFF / BOX 3 OF 7' wobbles, opens and throws out 'Oven warranty', 'Tile samples', 'Kitchen quote v3', 'Paint colours' (4.88–5.60); 'Not it.' stamp (5.60)
lines.delivery: 'Garage' flat, a beat, then 'box three of seven' a touch wearier, as if boxes one and two were a long afternoon. Out by 6.05.

lines.on_screen: 'SEARCH 14 · The ute.'; the glovebox drops open (6.36–6.60)
lines.delivery: Lowest and shortest of the three: she knows it's a long shot. Out by 7.05, as the receipt settles (6.96).

lines.on_screen: A bakery receipt rises out of the glovebox and holds clean: '1 x MINCE & CHEESE PIE $5.50' (6.54–6.96); 'Not it.' stamp (7.50); handwritten '(good pie though)' (7.80), held to the whip (8.50)
lines.delivery: The only warm line in the hunt. A small fond smile, under the breath, like remembering it. Out by 8.80, across the whip to the phone.

lines.on_screen: Generic text thread to 'Roofer · usually replies Sundays': Mon 9:12 am 'Need your Record of Work for the CCC, cheers' (8.82), Wed 4:40 pm 'Just bumping this' (9.44), Fri 7:05 am 'Any chance? (sorry, me again)' (10.10), 'Delivered' (10.36)
lines.delivery: One word per bubble: 'Monday' just after the first lands, then 'Wednesday', 'Friday', about 0.6 s apart. Patient, a bit sheepish by Friday, never annoyed. Out by 10.60.

lines.on_screen: Caption 'He's on a job in Queenstown. / Fair enough.' (10.72–12.68) under the thread
lines.delivery: Genuinely fair, no sarcasm: the roofer is not the joke, the paperwork is. 'Fair enough' warm and a little rueful. Out by 12.55, before the whip (12.68).
